:::{#exm-normal-density-max}
#### The peak of the Gaussian density grows as the standard deviation shrinks

By @thm-normal-density-max,
the peak of the [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) of $\ndist{0, \sigma^2}$ is $1 / (\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})$.
@fig-normal-density-max marks each peak for [standard deviations](variance-covariance.qmd#def-sd) $0.5$, $1$ and $2$.

```{r}
#| label: fig-normal-density-max
#| fig-cap: "Gaussian densities, with each peak marked"
#| fig-alt: "Three Gaussian curves; narrower ones peak higher."
#| code-fold: true

sds <- c(0.5, 1, 2)
x_grid <- seq(-6, 6, length.out = 400)
sd_label <- latex2exp::TeX("$\\sigma$")
density_label <- latex2exp::TeX("$f(x)$")

normal_curves <-
  dplyr::tibble(sd = sds) |>
  dplyr::reframe(.by = sd, x = x_grid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    density = dnorm(x, mean = 0, sd = sd),
    sd = factor(sd)
  )

normal_peaks <-
  dplyr::tibble(sd = sds) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    peak = 1 / (sd * sqrt(2 * pi)),
    sd = factor(sd)
  )

normal_plot <-
  normal_curves |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = density, col = sd) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = normal_peaks,
    ggplot2::aes(x = 0, y = peak)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(col = sd_label, y = density_label) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(normal_plot)
```

As $\sigma \to 0$, the peak $1 / (\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})$ grows indefinitely,
so a density can exceed $1$.

:::
